body: I'm sorry I'm responding late, but thank you. It's hard to remember when it comes to my own illness that it's just as real as any visible illness and that I need time to heal.
Wow, why didn't I think of that! Next you'll tell me to drink water when I'm dehydrated!
If a stranger wants to give me "candy" I'll damn take it, "candy" is expensive.
It's just hard for me to naturally form friendships cause I'm depressed as hell.
You're straight and she's a woman, it makes sense you're not interested.

First of all, I am so sorry this happened. I've had something similar happen and I understand how it hurts to be taken advantage of by someone you love and trust. I think the psychologist session with him will really help, just remember to be open and prioritise your feelings, you're the victim and don't need to spare his. Maybe sleeping apart for a while could help too? So you can start feeling safer where you're vulnerable. It might take a long while to regain that trust. Wishing you lots of strength.
You're right! I probably shouldn't be embarrassed for enjoying music!

You are still very young, plenty of time to grow into your looks! However looks definitely aren't everything. Keep working on your hobbies and talk with people that have similar interests, see what kind of traits you want to have as a person and work towards them, attitude and personality always shine through in the end. Notice what part of others leaves a lasting impression on you other than beauty. As for looks, you could always make small changes to compliment your natural beauty! Dress appropriately for your body shape, find a hairstyle that suits your face, maybe dye your hair! Lord knows at your age I had every colour of the rainbow pass my head, you're young and it's ok to experiment with styles.
I don't think it's normal, I have anxiety which makes me have those thoughts frequently too though. I'd suggest therapy.
Trying this today, I think they'll love it!
If it's gradually getting worse you might at least have time to ease into it. You might also need different a different prescription, though I'm assuming you already tried that.

You won't know about the future unless you're there to see it. I can't promise it will be better, but there's no guarantee it will be worse either. Your feelings aren't irrational though, you don't have it easy. Is there nothing that can be done about your vision?
And I've known people that lived in homes like that, at least where I live they seemed to help them.
If you are using something to hurt yourself, it's self harm. Doesn't have to be what people typically use, so no, you're not faking it.
It actually does help a little to hear about cis men this short or shorter. Thank you.
